primitives.name: Pinhole PTZ Camera Model
primitives.verbatim_quote: Method / model Camera modeled as pinhole: **P = K Q_φ Q_θ · S[I|-C]** where C is camera center, S is base rotation (time-invariant prior), Q_θ/Q_φ pan/tilt rotations, K intrinsic with square pixels and principal point at image center (focal length f only unknown).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'P': '3×4 projection matrix (dimensionless)', 'K': '3×3 intrinsic matrix (dimensionless)', 'Q_\\phi': '3×3 tilt rotation matrix (dimensionless)', 'Q_\\theta': '3×3 pan rotation matrix (dimensionless)', 'S': '3×3 base rotation matrix (dimensionless)', 'C': '3D camera center vector (meters)'}
primitives.assumptions: Fixed base orientation, pinhole camera model, square pixels, principal point at image center.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Narrow field of view (<25°) leads to high angular variance and reduced accuracy.

layer2.mapping: Maps 3D world coordinates to 2D image pixels via calibrated PTZ geometry; GSI uses this for event localization; GSE uses it for state transitions between field regions.
layer2.telemetry: Mean rotation error <1° in real-world tests, focal length error <2.5px.

primitives.verbatim_quote: Three steps: (1) focal length solved from two points via the image-of-absolute-conic quadratic (Gedikli et al.
primitives.assumptions: Two visible field markings, known image of absolute conic, planar field surface.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Insufficient field markings or non-planar surfaces invalidate solution.

primitives.name: SIFT Pan-Tilt Regression Forest
primitives.verbatim_quote: The paper proposes (a) a two-point annotation algorithm that uses prior knowledge of the PTZ camera's fixed base location/orientation, and (b) a "pan-tilt forest" (random forest regressing pan/tilt angles from SIFT patch descriptors) to calibrate new images without image-to-image feature matching.
primitives.assumptions: SIFT features are discriminable, forest trained on labeled pan/tilt pairs, fixed base assumption holds.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Low-quality SIFT features or insufficient training data reduce forest accuracy.

layer2.mapping: Enables fast pan-tilt estimation from image patches; GSI uses this for real-time tracking; GSE uses it for scene graph construction.
layer2.telemetry: Mean IoU 0.83 on real images, 0.95 target for NFL broadcast lanes.

The core innovation lies in extending traditional homography-based calibration to scenarios with fewer than four correspondences. By leveraging a fixed base assumption, the method solves for focal length using two points via the image of absolute conic (IoAC), then estimates pan/tilt using a single point. This is followed by a machine learning step where a random forest regressor maps SIFT descriptors to pan/tilt rays. The pinhole model P = K Q_φ Q_θ · S[I|-C] encapsulates the geometric transformation from 3D space to image plane. The IoAC-based focal length solver (step 1) relies on quadratic algebra derived from projective geometry. The pan/tilt estimation (step 2) uses closed-form trigonometric expressions. The forest regression (step 3) bridges visual features to angular estimates. Failure modes include narrow FOV (<25°), poor SIFT quality, and base rotation uncertainty. The method is robust to base-location errors but sensitive to base-rotation errors due to propagation from prior to PTZ components.
